overview: SPIRAL is a self-iterating autonomous development loop (Research  →  Implement  →  Validate). This PRD drives Spiral to improve itself: integrating newly-written lib modules into the main loop, enhancing the setup wizard to educate users about every configurable option, and adding Chrome DevTools-powered visual validation.
goals: Implement SPIRAL Phase G: auto-generate CHANGELOG.md and API docs from story commits using git-cliff and pdoc
Add comprehensive integration test suite that runs SPIRAL end-to-end with mock Claude API responses
Build SPIRAL self-monitoring dashboard: live token burn rate, story throughput, model escalation heatmap
Enable SPIRAL to support multi-repo projects: federated prd.json with sub-project story namespacing

userStories.title: Cost Predictor CLI: Estimate Pre-Phase I Story Costs Using results.tsv Historical Model
userStories.description: Add a predictive cost estimation CLI that analyzes historical results.tsv data to predict token consumption and cost for stories before Phase I implementation. Uses K-nearest neighbors on story attributes (complexity domain, total lines changed) to estimate costs for similar stories. Enables fast failure when cost would exceed remaining SPIRAL_COST_CEILING budget, reducing wasted tokens on oversized stories.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI: `spiral predict-cost --story-id US-123 --prd prd.json --history results.tsv` outputs JSON with {estimated_tokens: int, estimated_cost: float, confidence_pct: float, similar_stories: []}
Phase I calls predict-cost before decomposition; fails with clear error if estimated_cost > remaining budget (from .spiral/_checkpoint.json) and prevents story launch
Unit tests in tests/test_predict_cost.py: test_similar_story_lookup, test_confidence_calculation, test_budget_check_integration with >=48% coverage

userStories.title: Phase M: exclude completed stories from semantic dedup comparison set
userStories.description: Phase M currently compares every new story candidate against ALL stories in prd.json, including the 309+ completed ones (passes: true). This means a new story about 'improving X' gets rejected as a near-duplicate of the completed story 'implement X', even though they are genuinely different work. The dedup filter should only compare new candidates against PENDING stories (passes: false). Completed stories are done — a candidate that resembles a completed story is an extension or improvement, not a true duplicate. Fix lib/merge_stories.py (or the relevant dedup function): when building the comparison corpus, filter to only stories where passes is False.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase M dedup only compares new candidates against stories where passes == False
A new candidate with >85% title similarity to a completed (passes: true) story is NOT rejected as a duplicate
A new candidate with >85% title similarity to a pending (passes: false) story IS still rejected
uv run pytest tests/test_merge_stories.py covers the completed-story exclusion case
When prd.json has 300+ completed stories and 0 pending, Phase M merges new candidates normally
